209.text: Algorithm 1: Standard attention. Materializes the full N*N attention matrix in HBM (slow GPU memory). This is what everyone learned first, and it's the memory bottleneck FlashAttention eliminates.

218.text: Read the shapes off Q rather than the module globals. That one change is what lets the same three functions be called at the model's toy dimensions and at production dimensions in the scaling sweep below, with the counters staying comparable.

219.text: Count every read/write to "HBM" (slow memory) to make the cost explicit.

220.text: Read all of Q and K from HBM to compute the scores. Linear in N, and the cheapest part of what follows.

221.text: The O(N^2) matrix: every query against every key. This is the array the whole lab is about, and the only reason it fits here is that N is 7.

222.text: Write the full N x N score matrix out to HBM. This is the waste FlashAttention refuses to pay.

223.text: Build the causal mask: upper triangle blocks future positions.

224.text: Replace future-position scores with negative infinity. After softmax, these become zero, enforcing the causal left-to-right constraint.

225.text: Read the N x N matrix back in for the softmax — a full round trip through slow memory for data that was just written.

226.text: Row-wise softmax to get attention weights.

227.text: Write the N x N attention weights back out again. Second N^2 write of the forward pass.

228.text: Read the weights back one more time, plus all of V, to form the weighted sum. Three N^2 traversals so far, for an output that is only N x d.

229.text: Matrix multiply: attention weights * values = output.

230.text: Finally write the N x d output. Standard attention has now moved roughly 4 N^2 elements to produce it.

233.text: The largest single array this algorithm has to hold: the N x N score matrix, per head. Traffic counters are a proxy, but this is the number that decides whether a context length fits in memory at all.

240.text: Algorithm 2: Online softmax. Processes one key at a time, never materializing the N*N matrix. The foundation of FlashAttention, same output, far less memory traffic.

256.text: Same trick as in standard attention: shapes come from the tensor, so this runs unchanged at head_dim=4 and head_dim=64.

257.text: Track HBM operations, this algorithm has zero N*N writes.

258.text: Allocate output buffer, same shape as Q.

260.text: Heads are fully independent — no term in attention mixes them — so the outer loop is just bookkeeping.

262.text: Online softmax begins by loading one query row at a time. That is why memory use stays linear instead of materializing the whole attention matrix.

263.text: One query row read from HBM. Cheap; the expensive part is what this loop does to K and V.

265.text: The online softmax trick: maintain a running max, sum, and weighted output. No need to store all scores first.

266.text: Running sum of exp(scores) for softmax denominator.

267.text: The running weighted sum of values, accumulated incrementally. This head_dim vector is the entire working set of the algorithm — nothing here grows with N.

269.text: The inner loop streams over past keys and values only, matching the causal structure without ever storing an NxN score table.

270.text: Read one K and one V vector from HBM.

272.text: One K and one V vector, read from HBM. This is the line that costs: it re-reads all of K and V once per query row, which is the O(N^2 * d) traffic that makes online softmax a footprint fix rather than a traffic fix.

274.text: The dot product, scaled by sqrt(head_dim) so the softmax does not saturate as head width grows.

275.text: Track the running maximum so softmax can be updated stably as more keys arrive instead of needing the full row upfront.

278.text: Correction factor for when a new key raises the running max: everything accumulated so far was exponentiated against the old max and has to be rescaled. On the very first key running_max is -inf, so this is exp(-inf) = 0 and the accumulators start from scratch — no special case needed, which is why the old if is gone.

279.text: Rescale the running sum and add the new score's contribution.

280.text: Accumulate the weighted output incrementally alongside the running normalization terms. This is the core online-softmax trick.

281.text: Update the running max for the next iteration.

283.text: Only the final normalized output row is written back. The intermediate attention probabilities never hit main memory.

284.text: Only the final normalized output row is written. No N x N array was ever allocated, let alone written to HBM.

288.text: The largest intermediate is one head_dim accumulator. It does not depend on N at all, and that independence is the one thing this algorithm buys.

295.text: Algorithm 3: Tiled attention (FlashAttention). The best of both worlds: processes BLOCKS of keys at once (vectorized like standard) but never writes the N*N matrix (memory-efficient like online). This is what runs on real GPUs.

303.text: Same shape-from-tensor convention, so the tile size and the head dimension can both be swept.

304.text: Track HBM traffic and, separately, the peak allocation. Tiling wins on both, but for different reasons, so they are counted separately.

305.text: Column block size: how many keys to process at once.

306.text: Row block size: how many queries to process at once.

307.text: Allocate the output array with the same shape as Q to store attention results.

309.text: Heads are independent here too. In the real fused kernel this loop is the grid, not a loop.

310.text: Tile the query dimension into blocks of size Br.

311.text: Handle the last block which may be smaller.

312.text: Read a block of query vectors from slow HBM memory into fast on-chip SRAM, where all the compute for this tile happens.

313.text: How many rows in this query block.

314.text: Read a whole block of query rows at once, not one row. Everything downstream amortizes over Br queries.

316.text: Per-row running max for online softmax within this query block.

317.text: Running sum of exponentiated scores for each query row, used as the softmax denominator. Updated incrementally as new key blocks arrive.

318.text: One running output block, Br x d. Together with the score tile this is the algorithm's entire working set, sized to fit SRAM and independent of N.

320.text: Causal boundary: only attend to keys at or before the query positions.

321.text: Tile the key dimension into blocks of size Bc.

323.text: Read a block of key vectors from HBM into SRAM. Processing keys in blocks amortizes the memory transfer cost over many queries.

324.text: Read the corresponding block of value vectors alongside the keys, since both are needed to update the running output.

325.text: How many columns in this key block.

326.text: The K/V block read, amortized over block_cols positions and over every query row in the current block. This is the single difference from online softmax, and it is where the traffic win comes from.

328.text: One block matrix multiply: all queries in the tile against all keys in the tile. Same arithmetic as standard attention, arranged so the result never has to leave fast memory.

332.text: The biggest thing tiling ever allocates: one Br x Bc score tile plus the output accumulator. Both are chosen to fit in SRAM, and neither depends on N — which is why FlashAttention can run context lengths standard attention cannot fit.

335.text: Apply causal mask within this tile. Only positions where key <= query should contribute.

336.text: Walk through every query-key pair in the current tile to apply the causal mask where keys come after queries.

337.text: If the key position is after the query position, mask it out.

338.text: Replace causally invalid scores with a large negative value so softmax gives them zero weight, matching the standard attention mask.

341.text: Online softmax update across blocks, same math as Algorithm 2, but operating on entire blocks at once.

342.text: New running max: element-wise maximum of old max and this block's max.

343.text: Correction factor for previous blocks when the max increases.

344.text: Exponentiate scores relative to the new max.

346.text: Update running sum: rescale old sum, add new block's contribution.

347.text: Update running output: rescale old output, add new weighted values. This is the block version of the online softmax accumulation.

348.text: Update the running max for the next block.

350.text: Normalize by the final sum, completes the softmax computation for this query block.

351.text: Write out the finished output block. The N x N matrix never existed, so there is nothing else to flush.

457.text: Online softmax's closed form. The d * N * (N + 1) term is the whole story: K and V are streamed once per query row, so head_dim multiplies the quadratic term instead of sitting next to it.

460.text: Tiling's closed form, parameterized by tile size. K and V are read once per block of queries, so the quadratic term is divided by the number of blocks rather than by nothing.
